Id.description: A group or asset id: a ULID or a lowercase slug (ids name files, and macOS is case-insensitive). No '_', '/', '.', or '--'.

Handle.description: A person's unique, permanent name: shown as @handle, and the name of their people/<handle>/ directory.

GitId.description: A git commit or blob id.

DeviceName.description: A device's name within one person, such as 'macbook'.

TokenHash.description: The lowercase hex sha256 of a device token. Tokens are long random secrets, so the hash is safe to publish.

Device.description: A device a human uses opencorp from: requests carrying the token whose hash this is act as that person.

PasswordHash.description: A password's salted hash as a PHC string, such as $scrypt$ln=15,r=8,p=1$<salt>$<hash>; never the password itself.

ConnectionName.description: A connection's name on its office; `office` is office/provider.json. A removed name is never reused.

Timestamp.description: UTC, ISO-8601 in milliseconds with a Z suffix. Fixed width, so string order is time order; a plain string, so it round-trips unchanged.

devices.description: The devices this human uses opencorp from, each with a unique name.

password_hash.description: The hash of the password this human logs in a new device with; null for none.

model.description: A model id as a connection lists it, e.g. `gpt-5.5`, or `openai/gpt-4o` on OpenRouter. Each office starts the agent's chats on the first of its connections that offers it (the default first, then the others by name). If none does, it uses its default and says so in the chat.

who.description: A person's handle, or group:<group id>.

waiting_on.description: While status is waiting: who must act (answer an open question, or raise the cost cap), in the order those opened. Empty otherwise.

capped.description: True while the session's cost is at or over its cost cap: its turns wait until someone raises the cap, and its status is waiting.

opened_by.description: The human who opened the session; null for sessions from before this field or opened by the office itself.

connection.description: The chat's connection on its office. Null: `office`, for sessions from before this field; every new session sets it.

model.description: Null: the connection's own model. For Azure, a deployment name.

model_note.description: Why the chat isn't on the model it was asked to start on, or why it moved.

harness_model.description: The model the harness runs, as it reports it (a Codex session: Codex's load response); null until the harness reports it, and for composer sessions.

harness_usage.description: This session's own token counts so far, as the harness reports them. A continued session counts only its own stretch: add its parent chain's counts for the thread's total. Null until the harness reports any; always null for composer sessions.

parent_session_id.description: The session this one directly continues, on the same harness thread; follow its parent_session_id for earlier stretches. Null for a first stretch.

HarnessUsage.description: A harness session's token counts as the harness reports them, on the harness's own login; the office doesn't price them.

cached_input_tokens.description: The part of input_tokens served from the cache.

author.description: The human who sent a user message. A harness session names every sender; null for assistant messages, for composer sessions, and for rows from before this field.

ErrorPart.description: A turn that failed: why, in words the owner can act on. Never holds a secret.

secret.description: The answer is a secret: clients mask it, and the office stores `[secret]` in its place.

node_id.description: null for a model ask_user call.

source.description: harness: a request from the session's harness (a Codex approval or question). It takes only an `option` or `text` answer; no side chat, send back or stop. It goes `stale` when the harness stops waiting.

answer.description: null until answered, and may be null once answered too. Read status to tell whether it is answered.

failure.description: Why learning from it failed, when the office knows.

Event.description: A metadata change, written to the outbox.

data.description: The entity after the change; for company.updated, `{sha}` of the new company commit; for run.updated, a RunUpdated.

LiveEvent.description: Streamed content that is never stored as metadata. For part.delta, data is {message_id, part_id, text} and the text is appended.

connection.description: The human's pick of connection for the new chat, which falls back as the office decides; null leaves it to the office.

model.description: The human's pick of model for the new chat, which falls back as the office decides; null leaves it to the office.

CompanyView.description: The company at one commit of the office's clone, as GET /api/company serves it. People come without devices or password hashes.

company.description: Null when company.yaml is missing or doesn't parse at this commit.

issues.description: The files at this commit that don't parse.

CommitInfo.description: A commit of the office's clone of the company repo.

subject.description: The first line of the commit message.

author.description: The author's name, never their email.

CompanyTreeEntry.description: An entry (file, folder, symlink or submodule) of the company repo at one commit.

path.description: Repo-relative and /-separated, with no leading or trailing /.

size.description: The blob's size in bytes for a file or symlink; null for a folder or submodule.

CompanyTree.description: The company repo's files at HEAD of the office's clone, as GET /api/company/tree serves it.

entries.description: At most 5,000, taken breadth-first: by depth, then name.

truncated.description: True when entries past the cap were left out.

skipped.description: Paths left out because they aren't valid UTF-8, have a `.` or `..` segment, or would reveal a secret; they can't be read.

CompanyFile.description: One file of the company repo at a served commit, as GET /api/company/file serves it. Errors come as an ApiError: a malformed path gets 400 bad_path; a path that isn't in that commit's listing, or is a folder, gets 404 no_file; 409 stale_commit means `at` isn't one of the last 8 HEADs the office served, so refetch the tree.

path.description: Repo-relative and /-separated, with no leading or trailing /.

content.description: What the response holds: text in `text`, a symlink's target in `target`, a hidden file's reason in `reason`; nothing for the others.

text.description: The file's text, secrets removed, when content is text; else null.

target.description: Where the symlink points, shown and never followed, when content is symlink; else null.

reason.description: Why the file is hidden, a fixed message that never quotes the file, when content is hidden; else null.

rewritten.description: True when text is the file re-rendered from parsed YAML without its secret keys, so comments and layout aren't kept.

RunSummary.description: One run the office launched, as the Run Logs list shows it: from the office's runs table, the session, its questions and memory. No run log is read for it.

flow.description: What ran: chat, side_chat, profile_manager or debrief; later SOPs and discussions.

flow_path.description: The flow's path in the company repo, at the session's pinned commit.

person.description: The employee whose flow it is.

driver.description: Who started the run, fixed at launch: a human's handle, or `office` for runs the office starts itself.

participants.description: Everyone else in it, the employee first: whoever answered its turns, cards or questions, or opened a side chat on its cards. Never the driver.

parent_run_id.description: The run it was started from: a side chat's card's run, a debrief's session's last run. Null for a top-level run.

reason.description: Why it failed or was interrupted, secrets removed.

failed_node.description: The node it failed at, when it failed at one.

current_nodes.description: While running, waiting or idle: the node ids it is at now, deepest only. Empty while running means it is starting.

asking.description: While waiting: a model question (one with no node) is open.

held.description: While waiting: it is held at its cost cap, with nothing else open.

codex.description: A debrief of a Codex session.

ended_at.description: When the office learned it ended. Null while open, and for a run an office stop interrupted.

replaces.description: The run of the same session this fresh run replaced.

replaced_by.description: The fresh run of the same session that replaced this one.

children.description: On a top-level row of a list page and on a run's page: the newest 200 runs started from it, newest first.

children_total.description: How many runs were started from it, shown or not.

RunPage.description: One page of GET /runs: top-level runs, newest first, each with its children.

next.description: The `before` of the next page; null on the last.

RunUsage.description: What a run's model calls used, as the chat harness recorded them.

RunDetail.description: GET /runs/{id}: the run's summary, what its log's first record says, and whether the log can be read.

repo_commit.description: The session's pinned commit: which version of the flow ran.

learnable.description: Whether the log keeps evidence (prompts, model turns, tool calls); null until the log is read.

models.description: The model of each agent node, by static path, from the log's first record.

usage.description: Null when not recorded: the office records usage only for runs the chat harness runs, not debriefs.

log_message.description: What to show for any log_state but ok.

bytes_done.description: While indexing: bytes of the log read so far.

bytes_total.description: While indexing: the log's size in bytes.

RunNode.description: One node attempt, from its start record and its outcome record.

end_seq.description: The outcome record's seq; null while open or once restarted.

kind.description: agent, case, loop, map, call, …: the node's kind by static path. Always null until Yian lists a flow's nodes publicly (yian#943); clients show nothing for null.

handle.description: For a routed case: the handle it took.

error.description: For a failed node: its error, secrets removed.

RunDivider.description: A run_resumed record: where the run was resumed and which nodes it retried.

RunNodePage.description: GET /runs/{id}/nodes: node attempts, newest start first, and the resume dividers among them.

next_before.description: The `before` of the next (older) page; null on the oldest.

dropped.description: True when older attempts were dropped from the table (past 100,000): see Raw.

indexing.description: True when the log is still being read for the first time: nodes is empty; ask again.

bytes_done.description: While indexing: bytes of the log read so far.

bytes_total.description: While indexing: the log's size in bytes.

RunEvent.description: One run-log record as written, secrets removed.

payload.description: The record's payload, scrubbed; null when withheld or too large to preview.

cut.description: JSON pointers (into payload) of strings cut at 4 KiB; fetch the event by seq for the whole.

evidence_left_out.description: True when evidence was left out of a page; fetch the event by seq for it.

withheld.description: Why the payload isn't shown: a secret couldn't be removed.

size.description: The record's size in bytes, when it was too large to preview.

RunEventPage.description: GET /runs/{id}/events: records in seq order, at most 500 or 256 KiB of JSON.

next_after.description: The `after` of the next page; null at the end of the log so far.

cut.description: True when the page stopped at its byte cap.

indexing.description: True when the log is still being read for the first time: events is empty; ask again.

bytes_done.description: While indexing: bytes of the log read so far.

bytes_total.description: While indexing: the log's size in bytes.

RunUpdated.description: The data of a run.updated event: from the store and memory, node ids only.

usd.description: The price of the person's model calls since the report's start; only composer sessions are priced.

unpriced_sessions.description: The person's harness sessions (Codex, Claude) updated since then, whose tokens the office doesn't price.

CostReport.description: Spend per person since a time, as GET /costs and GET /api/costs serve it.

people.description: By handle; people with no spend are left out.

api.description: The compatibility key: `<version>+<first 12 hex of sha256(protocol.schema.json)>`, or just the version for an install without the schema.
The compatibility key the app was built for.

Health.description: GET /api/health: the office's compatibility key and the built app's, if there is one.

app.description: Null when the web app isn't built.

port.description: The bound port while listening, else the configured one.

HqStatus.description: GET /hq on the office socket: where HQ listens, for `opencorp pair` and `opencorp doctor`.

url.description: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ while TCP is listening, else null.

socket_error.description: Why hq.sock isn't listening, or null when it is.

PairCodeRequest.description: The body of POST /hq/pair on the office socket.

handle.description: The human the browser will act as; null: the asking person.

open_file.description: Also write a 0600 redirect file to open, so the code never appears in a process's arguments.

PairCode.description: A one-time pairing link: single use, valid for 5 minutes. `path` and `url` carry the secret code: served only on the office socket, never under `/api`, and never logged.

url.description: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/pair#<code> while TCP is listening, else null.

socket.description: The path of hq.sock, for an SSH forward.

open_file.description: The redirect file's path, when one was asked for and TCP is listening.

PairRequest.description: The body of POST /api/pair: the code from the link's fragment.

label.description: Free text naming the browser, such as 'Safari on Mac'.

BrowserSession.description: A browser signed in to this office's HQ. Local to the office; never the cookie's secret.

name.description: web-<6 characters>, made by the office.

via.description: pair: a code from `opencorp pair`; login: a password.

issued_by.description: Who ran `opencorp pair`, or the person who signed in with a password.

HqLoginRequest.description: The body of POST /api/login: a human's handle and password; the office answers with a browser session cookie. A wrong handle or password gets 401 `bad_credentials`; too many tries get 429 `too_many_attempts` with a Retry-After header; success returns a `BrowserSession`, as for /api/pair.

password.description: Checked, then dropped: never stored, logged, or echoed in an error.

label.description: Free text naming the browser, such as 'Safari on Mac'.

ApiError.description: The body of every error response, sent with its HTTP status.

error.description: A short code, such as not_implemented or not_found.

answer_kind.description: sent_back and interrupted are set only by the office.

run_id.description: null means the session's latest run.

LoginRequest.description: The body of POST /login: a human's handle and password, and the device to add to their devices once they check out.

SetPasswordRequest.description: The body of PUT /people/{handle}/password: the new password, which the office stores only as a hash.

Connection.description: A model connection on this office. Never holds a key.

can_manage.description: Whether the asking person may add, remove or set the default.

ModelOption.description: A model a connection offers; `name` is its display name when the provider gives one.

ModelList.description: `listed` false: the provider can't list models, so a model name is typed.

SetModelRequest.description: A model equal to the connection's own is stored as null, so it follows that connection's changes.

AddConnectionRequest.description: A new API-key connection. The office never echoes it: a 422 names fields only.

endpoint.description: Azure: the resource name or URL. provider openai: an OpenAI-compatible base URL.

StartLoginRequest.description: Starts a subscription sign-in that adds a connection.

ConnectionLogin.description: A subscription sign-in. While `waiting`, the human opens `url` and enters `user_code`; `connection` names the new connection once `signed_in`; `message` says why it failed.

SetupPrompt.description: One line `python -m opencorp.install init|onboard --json-prompts` writes on stdout: a question for `opencorp`'s setup screen, or something to show.

SetupAsk.description: A typed answer; an empty one means `default`.

SetupChoose.description: Pick one of `options`, or with `typed` type an answer.

typed.description: Whether the owner may type an answer of their own instead of picking one of `options`.

SetupSecret.description: An answer typed without being shown.

SetupAnswer.description: One line `opencorp`'s setup screen writes to the install's stdin: the answer to the last ask, choose or secret.
